newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo Motor's Indonesia expansion plans on hold.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo Motor's Indonesia expansion plans on hold.

text.p: Daewoo Motor Co Ltd has put on hold expansion plans in Indonesia because of competition from rival South Korean carmaker Kia Motors Corp, a company spokesman said on Monday.
"We have decided to put the plan on hold for now to refrain from unnecessary competition with Kia's 'national car' project in Indonesia," Lee Chang-won said.

Kia is making Timor cars in South Korea for export to Indonesia under a deal with PT Timor Putra Nasional, controlled by Indonesian President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra. Production eventually will shift to Indonesia.
Daewoo, South Korea's third largest carmaker and a subsidiary of the Daewoo Group DWGR.CN, is building 2,000 Espero cars each year in Indonesia in a 51 percent owned company, Starsauto Dinamika.
It announced in September 1995 it planned to build a second plant with annual production capacity of 20,000 passenger cars and 300 buses near Jakarta by the end of 1997.

"Kia appears to be doing well in Indonesia now. If Kia continues to be successful we may scrap the further investment plan," said Lee. "But we may decide to go ahead with the plan in the future if demand is there and problems occur with Kia's project."
